interpreterSource.note: Built with ./build-wasm.sh on Linux x86_64 (rust 1.97.1; the same bytes from a second path and target dir). Testnet only. The interpreter with DEPLOY-TIME LIMITS: __constructor(Limits) stores reads / leaves / bytes / elems / in entries / depth once in instance storage (each between a floor and a hard ceiling: reads 1..8, leaves 4..400, bytes 256..40,960, elems 2..64, in 1..64, depth 2..8, else error 220) and limits() returns them; install, check and enforce hold a predicate to them. This instance was deployed with reads 8, leaves 400, bytes 24,576 (PayFi's largest rule is 8.8 KB), elems 32, in 32, depth 5 (see `limits`). Nothing else deployed was touched.

note: Interpreter with deploy-time limits, testnet only. The deployer is a throwaway identity funded by friendbot. The pin in packages/policy-synth/src/config.ts names this address. The instance's limits are immutable: no setter, no upgrade path.

liveTests.note: An OZ smart account (rule 0: Default, no policy, one delegated signer: GAT7JHM4..., the deployer of the instances before this one) used by packages/policy-synth's live tests; the recorded RPC fixtures (packages/policy-synth/fixtures/rpc) replay against it. Rules 1 to 4 were installed on earlier interpreter instances (CDL7KHDK..., CA5ICI2O..., CAECFZWH..., CDZV4AG4...; installTx lists them by rule), so each reads as a rule policed by a known interpreter this build refuses to trust. Rule 5 was installed through the builder on this instance: `cap-500` on a made-up token, a cap of 500 on argument 2 of `transfer`, no pin, the same predicate as rules 2 and 4.

superseded.why: its wasm (69cad1d5...) is this source before the keyless executor rules for OpenZeppelin 0.8.0 (810f53f1...); policy-synth no longer trusts it
